concepts.name: Stages of hiring pipeline
concepts.summary: Recall the main steps from defining a role through sourcing, screening, interviewing, offer and onboarding.

concepts.name: Job description components
concepts.summary: Identify the parts of a job description such as responsibilities, required skills, level and location, and what each tells candidates.

concepts.name: Role requirements versus preferences
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between essential and desirable requirements and why mixing them narrows the candidate pool.

concepts.name: Common interview formats
concepts.summary: Name the common interview formats and what each is typically used to assess.

concepts.name: Purpose of interviews
concepts.summary: Explain that interviews gather evidence about job-relevant skills and fit for both sides, not just a gut impression.

concepts.name: Basic candidate preparation
concepts.summary: Understand why candidates research the company, review the role and prepare examples of past work.

concepts.name: Fair and lawful hiring basics
concepts.summary: Understand that decisions must rest on job-relevant criteria and that questions about protected characteristics are inappropriate.

misconceptions.text: A good interviewer can reliably judge a candidate from a gut feeling in the first few minutes.
Job descriptions should list every skill the team might ever want so candidates see the full picture.
Hiring starts when the first interview is scheduled.

concepts.name: Role scorecard drafting
concepts.summary: Turn a role into a short list of outcomes and competencies that can be assessed.

concepts.name: Sourcing channels
concepts.summary: Describe channels such as referrals, job boards and direct outreach and the trade-offs in reach and quality of each.

concepts.name: Resume screening against criteria
concepts.summary: Screen applications against written criteria rather than impressions like school or past employer prestige.

concepts.name: Behavioural question construction
concepts.summary: Write questions that ask for specific past situations tied to a competency.

concepts.name: STAR answer structuring
concepts.summary: Structure candidate answers as situation, task, action and result, with concrete outcomes.

concepts.name: Structured note-taking
concepts.summary: Record what the candidate said and did separately from your interpretation.

concepts.name: Candidate experience basics
concepts.summary: Explain how clear timelines, prompt feedback and respectful conduct affect acceptance and employer reputation.

misconceptions.text: Candidates from well-known companies or universities are automatically stronger.
Any question asked in an interview counts as a behavioural question.
A STAR answer is simply a story, and polish matters more than the specifics of the action taken.

concepts.name: Structured interview design
concepts.summary: Design an interview loop where each stage covers specific competencies with the same questions for every candidate.

concepts.name: Scoring rubrics with anchors
concepts.summary: Build rubrics with defined behavioural anchors so ratings are comparable across interviewers.

concepts.name: Bias mitigation in hiring
concepts.summary: Analyse where halo effect, similarity bias and anchoring enter the process and apply controls such as blind screening and independent scoring.

concepts.name: Work sample assessments
concepts.summary: Design realistic, time-bounded tasks that mirror the job and evaluate them against the rubric.

concepts.name: Debrief and decision meeting
concepts.summary: Run a debrief where interviewers submit written ratings first and then compare evidence on each competency.

concepts.name: Interviewer probing technique
concepts.summary: Use follow-ups to separate personal contribution from team outcomes and to test depth.

concepts.name: Pipeline metrics analysis
concepts.summary: Interpret stage conversion, time-to-hire and drop-off to locate bottlenecks or inequities.

misconceptions.text: Structured interviews are rigid and less predictive than free-flowing conversations.
Being aware of your biases is enough to prevent them affecting your ratings.
The debrief should start with the most senior person's opinion to save time.

concepts.name: Predictive validity of methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate selection methods by evidence on how well they predict job performance and decide how to combine them.

concepts.name: Interviewer calibration
concepts.summary: Analyse rating differences across interviewers and correct them with training, shadowing and feedback.

concepts.name: Adverse impact analysis
concepts.summary: Assess whether stages screen out groups disproportionately and judge whether the criterion is job-related.

concepts.name: Level and role calibration
concepts.summary: Distinguish scope, autonomy and impact across levels so candidates are assessed and placed consistently.

concepts.name: Offer and negotiation strategy
concepts.summary: Judge offer structure, leveling and negotiation approach balancing internal equity, budget and candidate motivations.

concepts.name: Evaluating borderline candidates
concepts.summary: Weigh conflicting evidence, decide whether to gather more data and justify a hire or no-hire.

concepts.name: Strategic candidate positioning
concepts.summary: As a candidate, analyse the interviewers' criteria and tailor evidence, questions and negotiation to them.

misconceptions.text: Unstructured conversation about culture fit is the best predictor of success.
If no protected-group differences were intended, the process cannot have adverse impact.
Hiring a borderline candidate is fine because they can grow into the role.

concepts.name: Hiring system design
concepts.summary: Design a hiring system aligned with workforce planning, covering roles, methods, tooling and governance.

concepts.name: Selection process validation
concepts.summary: Evaluate a company's own process by linking assessment scores to later performance and retention.

concepts.name: Trade-off assessment of speed and rigour
concepts.summary: Judge how much assessment is justified by role risk and market conditions.

concepts.name: Interview question bank creation
concepts.summary: Create validated question sets, exercises and rubrics for new roles.

concepts.name: Hiring culture and governance
concepts.summary: Build norms, accountability and incentives that sustain a consistent hiring bar and fair practice across teams.

concepts.name: Impact of AI in screening
concepts.summary: Evaluate automated screening and assessment tools for validity, bias and transparency before adopting them.

concepts.name: Executive and rare-skill hiring
concepts.summary: Create tailored approaches for senior or scarce-talent roles, including references, search partners and stakeholder alignment.

misconceptions.text: A vendor's claim that a screening algorithm is bias-free removes the need to audit it.
A rigorous process is always worth its cost, whatever the role and market.
A strong hiring bar comes from hiring only exceptional people, not from consistent process and accountability.
